name: Supply Chain Management
description: Third year, compulsory, 3 ECTS, 15 sessions, Operations and Business Analytics area
professors: Luis Vivanco de Mária y Campos
syllabusProgramme:
PROGRAM
SESSION 1 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Learn about introductory examples of sustainable supply
chain management practices.
Fundamentals of Supply Chain Management
Learning Objectives:
Understand the goal and scope of supply chain management and the
problems it addresses in modern organizations.
Identify the flows of products, information, and funds and explain how they
connect activities within and across firms.
Distinguish Operations Management and Supply Chain Management and
explain how they complement each other.
Understand the responsibilities, decision scope, and required skills of supply
chain managers.
Understand the course structure, evaluation criteria, and expectations.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 1: Understanding the supply chain) (See
Bibliography) (N/C)
SESSION 2 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Learn the importance of achieving supply chain fit between
a company’s supply chain strategy and its sustainability strategy.
Strategic Fit in a Supply Chain
Learning Objectives:
Explain the concept of strategic fit between a firm’s competitive strategy and
its supply chain strategy.
Differentiate between functional and innovative products and their
implications for supply chain design.
Understand how to align supply chains with demand and supply uncertainty
(efficient, risk-hedging, responsive, agile).
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 2: Achieving Strategic Fit in a Supply Chain)
(See Bibliography) (N/C)
Article: ALIGNING SUPPLY CHAIN STRATEGIES WITH PRODUCT UNCERTAINTIES (CMR230-PDF-ENG)
SESSION 3 (ASYNCHRONOUS)
Sustainability Topics: Understand how companies improve supply chain
sustainability through supply chain coordination.
Supply Chain Coordination I
Learning Objectives:
Explain why coordination failures arise in supply chains.
Identify the main drivers of the bullwhip effect and their impact on
performance.
Analyse the role of information delays and incentive misalignment in demand
distortion.
Apply coordination concepts to manufacturing and service settings.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 10: Coordination in a Supply Chain) (See
Bibliography) (N/C)
Games & Simulations: IE Supply Chain Simulation (OPE090090-U-ENG-HTM)
Article: BULLWHIP EFFECT IN SUPPLY CHAINS (SMR029-PDF-ENG)
SESSION 4 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Understand how companies improve supply chain
sustainability through supply chain coordination.
Supply Chain Coordination II
Learning Objectives:
Evaluate how contracts and incentives can improve coordination across
supply chain partners.
Explain the role of information sharing and collaboration mechanisms (e.g.,
CPFR).
Recognize behavioral and organizational barriers to effective coordination.
Interpret insights from cases and simulations to assess coordination
outcomes.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 10: Coordination in a Supply Chain) (See
Bibliography) (N/C)
Article: BULLWHIP EFFECT IN SUPPLY CHAINS (SMR029-PDF-ENG)
SESSION 5 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Understand how supply chain network design decisions
contribute to building a sustainable supply chain.
Supply Chain Network Design
Learning Objectives:
Understand key network design decisions related to facility location,
capacity, and allocation.
Analyse cost-service trade-offs in supply chain network configurations.
Apply network design concepts to both manufacturing and service supply
chains.
Interpret how network design supports overall supply chain strategy.
SESSION 6 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Understand the importance of sustainable sourcing from
both environmental and social perspectives.
Procurement and Sourcing Strategy
Learning Objectives:
Evaluate suppliers using multiple performance and risk criteria.
Apply the Kraljic portfolio logic to segment sourcing strategies.
Understand how sustainability considerations influence sourcing decisions.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 15: Sourcing Decisions in a Supply Chain)
(See Bibliography) (N/C)
SESSION 7 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Examine how global sourcing and capacity decisions
shape the sustainability of supply chains.
Global Sourcing, Capacity, and Risk
Learning Objectives:
Analyse challenges of outsourced production and global sourcing.
Compare reactive and speculative capacity strategies under demand
uncertainty.
Evaluate how incentives and risk-sharing mechanisms shape supplier
behavior.
Identify major risks in global sourcing and their managerial implications.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 6: Designing Global Supply Chain Networks)
(See Bibliography) (N/C)
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 15: Sourcing Decisions in a Supply Chain)
(See Bibliography) (N/C)
SESSION 8 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Study how companies adopt sustainable transportation
modes and logistics networks to reduce environmental impacts.
Transportation and Logistics I
Learning Objectives:
Compare transportation modes based on cost, speed, reliability, and
emissions.
Understand how logistics network structures affect responsiveness and
efficiency.
Evaluate trade-offs in transportation decisions, including last-mile
considerations.
Recognize logistics challenges in both manufacturing and service contexts.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 14: Transportation in a Supply Chain) (See
Bibliography) (N/C)
SESSION 9 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Study how reverse logistics create both environmental
benefits and organizational competitiveness.
Transportation and Logistics II
Learning Objectives:
Explain the role of reverse logistics in modern supply chains.
Compare alternatives for returns, reuse, refurbishing, recycling, and disposal.
Analyse economic and environmental trade-offs in reverse flows.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 14: Transportation in a Supply Chain) (See
Bibliography) (N/C)
SESSION 10 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Understand how resilient supply chains support long-term
sustainability.
Supply Chain Disruption and Resilience
Learning Objectives:
Identify major sources of supply chain disruptions in global environments.
Analyse resilience challenges in manufacturing and service supply chains.
Explain key resilience strategies to address supply chain disruptions.
Evaluate trade-offs between efficiency and robustness.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 6: Designing Global Supply Chain Networks)
(See Bibliography) (N/C)
Article: Supply Chain View of the Resilient Enterprise (SMR185-PDF-ENG)
SESSION 11 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Sustainability Topics: Examine how emerging trends in supply chain
management influence environmental sustainability.
Emerging Trends and Challenges in Supply Chain Management
Learning Objectives:
Explore emerging trends and challenges in supply chain management.
Analyse how technology, digitalization, and sustainability reshape supply
chains.
Connect current issues to core SCM frameworks introduced earlier in the
course.
Critically assess managerial implications of contemporary SCM
developments.
Book Chapters: Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation (Chapter 17: Sustainability and the Supply Chain)
(See Bibliography) (N/C)
Course materials will be provided based on the professor’s selected topic.
SESSIONS 12 - 13 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Final Group Presentations
Learning Objectives:
Apply SCM concepts and frameworks to a real or realistic supply chain
problem.
Demonstrate integrated, system-level thinking across supply chain functions.
Communicate analysis and recommendations clearly and persuasively.
Engage in constructive discussion and feedback.
SESSION 14 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Course Wrap-Up and Final Exam Preparation
Learning Objectives:
Synthesize key insights from across the course into a coherent framework.
Reflect on SCM’s role in manufacturing and service industries.
Strengthen the ability to apply course concepts to exam-style questions.
Clarify expectations for the final exam.
SESSION 15 (LIVE IN-PERSON)
Final Exam
